original_question: In the Young-Fibonacci lattices YF_r, do there exist sequences of elements (p_i)_{i >= 0} such that for every n the intervals [p_n, p_{n+k}] are all isomorphic as k varies, and if such sequences exist can they be used to prove an analog of the interval-stability result described in the paper and thereby suggest a semi-distributive property of YF_r?
target_in_paper: Problem 43 in Section 2 ("Problems of 2025") of arXiv:2509.25446.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right object (the Young–Fibonacci lattices YF_r), the right structural phenomenon to look for (a sequence p_0,p_1,p_2,\dots with stable interval types), and the right intended payoff from the paper’s context: using such a sequence to mimic the Liang–Sagan argument and to look for a semidistributive-type shadow of the distributive-lattice method.
missing_details: The paper’s nearest official formulation is an open problem, namely Problem 43, not a theorem or conjecture stated elsewhere.
The positive integer parameter r should be fixed explicitly: one asks the question for a fixed r>0 in the r-differential Young–Fibonacci lattice YF_r.
The sequence should be specified as an infinite ascending chain in the poset order, e.g. p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots.

The interval-isomorphism quantifiers need to be made precise. As written, "for every n the intervals [p_n,p_{n+k}] are all isomorphic as k varies" is ambiguous; the coherent paper-faithful interpretation is that for each fixed gap k>=0, the intervals [p_n,p_{n+k}] are pairwise isomorphic as n varies, i.e. the interval type depends only on k.
It should be stated that the intervals are closed intervals in the poset order and are required to be isomorphic as posets.
The paper does not ask for an analog of an "interval-stability theorem" as such; rather, Problem 43 asks whether such interval stability can be used to prove an analog of Liang–Sagan’s Theorem 3.1.

To make the question stand-alone, the analog of Theorem 3.1 should be named explicitly: a log-concavity statement for the interval-cardinality sequence a_k = #[p_0,p_k] (equivalently, any #[p_n,p_{n+k}] if the interval type depends only on k).
The Liang–Sagan mechanism being imported is their Order Ideal Lemma argument, so a faithful reformulation should indicate that this is the intended method being mirrored.
The phrase "semi-distributive property" is only heuristic in Problem 43; the paper does not define a specific semidistributive axiom or formal property to be proved.
No ambient ring, field, operators, degree conditions, homogeneity assumptions, or nilpotency hypotheses are relevant here; this is a purely poset/lattice-theoretic question.
refined_question: Fix r in Z_{>0}. In the r-differential Young–Fibonacci lattice YF_r, does there exist an infinite chain p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots such that, for every k >= 0, the closed intervals [p_n, p_{n+k}] are pairwise isomorphic as posets for all n >= 0? If such a chain exists, can it be used, in the same role that the translated partitions lambda+n play in Young’s lattice, to prove a Young–Fibonacci analogue of Liang–Sagan’s Theorem 3.1—namely, that the interval-cardinality sequence a_k := #[p_0, p_k] is log-concave—and would such a result suggest some semidistributive-type property of YF_r?
justification: This draft is targeting Problem 43 exactly. Problem 43 explicitly singles out the Liang–Sagan interval-shift phenomenon in Young’s lattice, explains that it is used to apply the Order Ideal Lemma, and then asks whether an analogous phenomenon exists in YF_r and whether it would lead to an analog of Liang–Sagan’s Theorem 3.1 together with evidence for a semidistributive-type property. The nearby cited context shows that Liang–Sagan’s Lemma 1.1 is the Order Ideal Lemma and that their Theorem 3.1 is a log-concavity statement for the sequence n mapsto #[lambda, lambda+n]. So the sharp paper-faithful reformulation must (i) state the interval-stability condition with correct quantifiers, and (ii) identify the desired conclusion as a log-concavity analogue, not merely as a vague interval-stability result.
